label: lem:profile-compactness
title: Lemma
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
For $a\in\mathbb S^{n-1}$, set $A_a\coloneqq I+(p-2)a\otimes a$. Since
\[
  I\le A_a\le(p-1)I,
\]
equation \eqref{eq:Fq} implies that every normalized shifted solution satisfies
\[
  -\left\lvert Dv+q\right\rvert^{p-2}\mathcal M^+(D^2v)\le0,
  \qquad
  -\left\lvert Dv+q\right\rvert^{p-2}\mathcal M^-(D^2v)\ge0
  \quad\text{in }B_1,
\]
where $\mathcal M^\pm$ are the Pucci extremal operators with ellipticity constants $1$ and $p-1$. These inequalities hold in the full viscosity sense, since the factor vanishes at tests with $D\phi+q=0$. Applying the cutting lemma of \cite[Lemma~6]{ImbertSilvestre2013} separately to the subsolution and supersolution inequalities gives
\[
  -\mathcal M^+(D^2v)\le0,
  \qquad
  -\mathcal M^-(D^2v)\ge0
  \quad\text{in }B_1.
\]
Thus, every normalized shifted solution belongs to the same Pucci class, independently of $q$. The Krylov--Safonov interior H\"older estimate, see \cite{CaffarelliCabre1995}, therefore gives $\sigma=\sigma(n,p)\in(0,1)$ and $C=C(n,p)$ such that
\[
  [v]_{C^{0,\sigma}(B_{3/4})}\le C.
\]
Thus every $v\in\mathcal K_0$ satisfies
\[
  \left\lVert v\right\rVert_{C(\overline B_{1/2})}\le1,
  \qquad
  \left\lvert v(x)-v(y)\right\rvert\le C\left\lvert x-y\right\rvert^{\sigma}
  \quad\text{for all }x,y\in\overline B_{1/2},
\]
and this extends to every $h\in\mathcal K$ by uniform convergence. Hence $\mathcal K$ is uniformly bounded and equicontinuous on $\overline B_{1/2}$. By Arzel\`a--Ascoli, every sequence in $\mathcal K$ has a subsequence converging uniformly on $\overline B_{1/2}$. Since $\mathcal K$ is closed in $C(\overline B_{1/2})$ by definition, the limit belongs to $\mathcal K$. This proves compactness in the uniform topology.

Fix $h\in\mathcal K$. By the definition of $\mathcal K$, there are sequences $q_j\in\mathbb R^n$ and $v_j\in C(B_1)$ such that
\[
  \mathcal F_{q_j}(Dv_j,D^2v_j)=0\quad\text{in }B_1, \qquad \left\lVert v_j\right\rVert_{L^\infty(B_1)}\le1,
\]
in the viscosity sense, and
\[
  \left\lVert v_j-h\right\rVert_{C(\overline B_{1/2})}\longrightarrow0.
\]
Passing to a subsequence, we may assume that either $q_j\to q\in\mathbb R^n$ or $\left\lvert q_j\right\rvert\to\infty$.
In the first case, $u_j\coloneqq v_j+q_j\cdot x$ is $p$-harmonic by \Cref{lem:equivalence}, and $u_j\to h+q\cdot x$ locally uniformly. The local-uniform stability of $p$-harmonic functions therefore shows that $h+q\cdot x$ is weakly $p$-harmonic.

In the second case, passing to a further subsequence, $q_j/\left\lvert q_j\right\rvert\to e\in\mathbb S^{n-1}$. Hence
\[
  \mathcal F_{q_j}(\xi,X)\longrightarrow
  -\operatorname{tr}\bigl((I+(p-2)e\otimes e)X\bigr)
\]
locally uniformly in $(\xi,X)\in\mathbb R^n\times\operatorname{Sym}(n)$. By viscosity stability, $h$ satisfies
\[
  -\operatorname{tr}\bigl((I+(p-2)e\otimes e)D^2h\bigr)=0
  \quad\text{in }B_{1/2}.
\]
This proves the alternatives.

label: lem:holder-flatness
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:holder-flatness}
Assume the qualitative regularity hypothesis of \Cref{thm:intro-principle}, and let $0<\beta<\gamma$. Then there exists an integer $N\ge1$ and pairs
\[
(\rho_i,b_i)\in(0,1/4)\times\mathbb R^n,\qquad 1\le i\le N,
\]
such that, for every $q\in\mathbb R^n$ and every viscosity solution
\[
\mathcal F_q(Dv,D^2v)=0\quad\text{in }B_1,\qquad \left\lVert v\right\rVert_{L^\infty(B_1)}\le1,
\]
there is an index $i\in\{1,\ldots,N\}$ for which
\begin{equation}\label{eq:holder-one-step}
\left\lVert v-v(0)-b_i\cdot x\right\rVert_{L^\infty(B_{\rho_i})}<\frac14\rho_i^{1+\beta}.
\end{equation}
head: environment

label: eq:holder-profile-strict
title: Proof
body_md:
We construct a relatively open covering of $\mathcal K$. Fix $h\in\mathcal K$. By \Cref{lem:profile-compactness} and the qualitative regularity hypothesis, $h\in C^{1,\gamma}_{\mathrm{loc}}(B_{1/2})$. Indeed, in the first alternative, it differs from a $p$-harmonic function by an affine function, while in the second alternative, it is smooth. Set
\[
\ell_h(x)\coloneqq h(0)+Dh(0)\cdot x.
\]
Since $\beta<\gamma$, we may choose $\rho_h\in(0,1/4)$ so small that
\begin{equation}\label{eq:holder-profile-strict}
\left\lVert h-\ell_h\right\rVert_{L^\infty(B_{\rho_h})}\le[Dh]_{C^{0,\gamma}(B_{1/4})}\rho_h^{1+\gamma}<\frac18\rho_h^{1+\beta}.
\end{equation}
Define
\begin{equation}\label{eq:holder-open-set}
\mathcal O_h\coloneqq\left\{z\in\mathcal K:\left\lVert z-\ell_h\right\rVert_{L^\infty(B_{\rho_h})}<\frac18\rho_h^{1+\beta}\right\}.
\end{equation}
The map $z\mapsto\left\lVert z-\ell_h\right\rVert_{L^\infty(B_{\rho_h})}$ is continuous in the uniform norm on $C(\overline B_{1/2})$, so $\mathcal O_h$ is relatively open in $\mathcal K$. Moreover, \eqref{eq:holder-profile-strict} gives $h\in\mathcal O_h$. Thus $\{\mathcal O_h:h\in\mathcal K\}$ is a relatively open covering of $\mathcal K$.

By compactness, choose a finite subcovering $\mathcal O_{h_1},\ldots,\mathcal O_{h_N}$, and set
\[
\rho_i\coloneqq\rho_{h_i},\qquad b_i\coloneqq Dh_i(0).
\]
Let $v$ be any normalized shifted solution as in the statement. Its restriction to $\overline B_{1/2}$ belongs to $\mathcal K_0\subset\mathcal K$, and hence it lies in some $\mathcal O_{h_i}$. Since $\ell_{h_i}(0)=h_i(0)$, we obtain
\[
\begin{aligned}
\left\lVert v-v(0)-b_i\cdot x\right\rVert_{L^\infty(B_{\rho_i})}
&\le\left\lVert v-\ell_{h_i}\right\rVert_{L^\infty(B_{\rho_i})}+\left\lvert v(0)-h_i(0)\right\rvert\\
&\le2\left\lVert v-\ell_{h_i}\right\rVert_{L^\infty(B_{\rho_i})}
<\frac14\rho_i^{1+\beta}.
\end{aligned}
\]
This proves \eqref{eq:holder-one-step}.

title: Proof
body_md:
Fix $0<\beta<\alpha_{\mathrm{IM}}(p)$. By local boundedness,
\[
M\coloneqq\left\lVert u\right\rVert_{L^\infty(B_{3/4})}\le C(p)\left\lVert u\right\rVert_{L^p(B_1)}.
\]
Applying \Cref{thm:intro-principle} to $u$, with $\gamma=\alpha_{\mathrm{IM}}(p)$, and using $\left\lVert u\right\rVert_{L^\infty(B_{1/2})}\le M$, gives
\[
\left\lVert u\right\rVert_{C^{1,\beta}(B_{1/2})}\le C(p,\beta)M \le C(p,\beta)\left\lVert u\right\rVert_{L^p(B_1)},
\]
proving \eqref{eq:intro-planar-Lp}.

label: infq:small-gradient
title: Lemma
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Let
\[
 \mathcal K_\infty
 =\overline{\{v|_{\overline B_{1/2}}:v\in\mathcal N\}}^{\,C^1(\overline B_{1/2})},
 \qquad
 \mathcal Z_\infty=\{h\in\mathcal K_\infty:Dh(0)=0\}.
\]
Estimate~\eqref{infq:baseline} gives uniform bounds and equicontinuity for the functions and their gradients on $\overline B_{1/2}$. Arzel\`a--Ascoli therefore makes $\mathcal K_\infty$ compact in $C^1(\overline B_{1/2})$. The map $h\mapsto Dh(0)$ is continuous, so $\mathcal Z_\infty$ is compact as well. Every $h\in\mathcal K_\infty$ satisfies $h(0)=0$ and is infinity-harmonic in $B_{1/2}$, by the stability of viscosity solutions for the continuous operator $(\xi,X)\mapsto\langle X\xi,\xi\rangle$; see \cite[Section~6]{CrandallIshiiLions1992}.

For $h\in\mathcal Z_\infty$, qualitative regularity gives 
\[
   |h(x)| \le  H_h|x|^{4/3},\qquad x\in B_{1/4},
\]
where \(H_h=[Dh]_{C^{0,1/3}(B_{1/4})}\), and we used that $h(0) = |Dh(0)| = 0$. The strict inequality $\beta<1/3$ allows us to choose $\rho_h\in(0,1/8)$ such that
\[
 \|h\|_{L^\infty(B_{\rho_h})}
 <\tfrac12\rho_h^{1+\beta}.
\]
Thus, the relatively open sets
\[
 O_h=\{z\in\mathcal K_\infty:
          \|z\|_{L^\infty(B_{\rho_h})}<\rho_h^{1+\beta}\}
\]
cover $\mathcal Z_\infty$. Choose a finite subcover $O_{h_1},\ldots,O_{h_N}$ and put $O=\bigcup_{i=1}^N O_{h_i}$ and $\rho_i=\rho_{h_i}$.

If $\mathcal K_\infty\setminus O$ is nonempty, compactness and its disjointness from $\mathcal Z_\infty$ imply
\[
 m:=\min_{z\in\mathcal K_\infty\setminus O}|Dz(0)|>0.
\]
Set $\eta=\min\{1/2,m/2\}$. If the complement is empty, set $\eta=1/2$. In either case, $v\in\mathcal N$ and $|Dv(0)|\le\eta$ imply $v|_{\overline B_{1/2}}\in O$, which is precisely~\eqref{infq:improvement}.

label: infq:noncritical
title: Lemma
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $a=|Dv(0)|$. By~\eqref{infq:baseline}, $\eta\le a\le C_0$. Choose an orthogonal matrix $T$ with $Te_1=Dv(0)/a$, and set
\[
 L_0=C_0(4\sqrt2)^{1+\alpha_0},\qquad
 \lambda_\eta=
 \min\left\{\frac1{32},
       \left(\frac{\varepsilon_*\eta}{2L_0}\right)^{1/\alpha_0}\right\}.
\]
For $x\in Q_4$, define
\[
 w(x)=\frac{v(\lambda_\eta Tx)}{a\lambda_\eta}.
\]
The inclusion $\lambda_\eta TQ_4\subset B_{1/2}$ follows from $4\sqrt2\lambda_\eta<1/2$. Hence $w$ is infinity-harmonic in $Q_4$, and $w(0)=0$, $Dw(0)=e_1$. Applying~\eqref{infq:baseline} along segments gives
\[
 |v(y)-Dv(0)\cdot y|
 \le\frac{C_0}{1+\alpha_0}|y|^{1+\alpha_0},
 \quad y\in B_{1/2}.
\]
Consequently,
\[
 \|w-x_1\|_{L^\infty(Q_4)}
 \le\frac{L_0}{\eta}\lambda_\eta^{\alpha_0}
 \le\frac{\varepsilon_*}{2}<\varepsilon_*.
\]
By~\eqref{infq:near-affine}, $[Dw]_{C^{0,1/3}(Q_1)}\le M_*$. Since $B_1\subset Q_1$ and
\[
 Dw(x)=a^{-1}T^{\mathsf T}Dv(\lambda_\eta Tx),
\]
we obtain
\[
 [Dv]_{C^{0,1/3}(B_{\lambda_\eta})}
 \le aM_*\lambda_\eta^{-1/3}
 \le C_0M_*\lambda_\eta^{-1/3}.
\]
This proves~\eqref{infq:noncritical-estimate}, with $A_\eta=C_0M_*\lambda_\eta^{-1/3}$.

label: lem:nonlocal-approximation
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:nonlocal-approximation}
Assume the differentiability hypothesis of \Cref{thm:nonlocal-conditional}. There exist $K\ge2$ and $0<\theta<\rho_*<1/(4K)$, depending only on $n$ and $s$, with the following property: for every $q\in\mathbb R^n$ and every solution $v$ of \eqref{eq:nonlocal-shifted} satisfying
\[
\left\lvert v(x)\right\rvert\le\max\{1,\left\lvert x\right\rvert^{1+\alpha_1}\}, \quad x\in\mathbb R^n,
\]
there exist $r\in[\theta,\rho_*]$ and $b\in\mathbb R^n$, with $\left\lvert b\right\rvert\le L$, such that
\begin{equation}\label{eq:nonlocal-affine-approximation}
\left\lVert v-v(0)-b\cdot x\right\rVert_{L^\infty(B_{Kr})}<\frac r8.
\end{equation}
Moreover, the rescaled function
\[
w(x)\coloneqq\frac8r\bigl(v(rx)-v(0)-rb\cdot x\bigr)
\]
satisfies \(\left\lvert w(x)\right\rvert\le\max\{1,\left\lvert x\right\rvert^{1+\alpha_1}\}\), for \(x \in \mathbb R^n\).

label: eq:nonlocal-choice-of-scales
title: Proof
body_md:
We construct an open covering of a compact family of global solutions. Choose $K\ge2$ and $\rho_*\in(0,1/(4K))$ so that
\begin{equation}\label{eq:nonlocal-choice-of-scales}
K^{\alpha_1}\ge16L,
\qquad 8\cdot2^{\alpha_1}(4+L)\rho_*^{\alpha_1}\le1.
\end{equation}
Define
\begin{equation*}
  \mathcal K \coloneqq
  \left\{
    h \colon \mathbb R^n \to \mathbb{R} \ : \
    \begin{array}{l}
      h(0)=0, \quad [h]_{C^{0,1}(\mathbb R^n)}\le L, \\[2pt]
      \left\lvert Dh+q\right\rvert(-\Delta)^s h=0 \ \text{in } \mathbb R^n,
      \quad \text{for some } q\in\mathbb R^n
    \end{array}
  \right\}.
\end{equation*}
This family is compact in the locally uniform topology of $\mathbb R^n$. Indeed, the bound $\left\lvert h(x)\right\rvert\le L\left\lvert x\right\rvert$ gives subsequential convergence by Arzel\`a--Ascoli, and dominated convergence gives convergence in $L_s^1(\mathbb R^n)$, since $2s>1$. For a sequence with shifts $q_j$, pass to a further subsequence such that either $q_j\to q$ or $\left\lvert q_j\right\rvert\to\infty$. In the first case, stability gives the shifted equation for the limit. In the second case, dividing the viscosity inequalities by the nonzero shifted gradient factors gives $(-\Delta)^sh=0$ in the limit, which belongs to $\mathcal K$ with shift zero, see \cite[Lemma~4.3]{CaffarelliSilvestre2011}. Moreover, every $h\in\mathcal K$ is differentiable at the origin by the hypothesis applied to $h+q\cdot x$, and $\left\lvert Dh(0)\right\rvert\le L$.

For each $h\in\mathcal K$, choose $\rho_h\in(0,\rho_*)$ such that
\[
\left\lVert h-Dh(0)\cdot x\right\rVert_{L^\infty(B_{K\rho_h})}<\frac{\rho_h}{8},
\]
and define the open set
\[
\mathcal O_h\coloneqq\left\{z\in C(\overline B_{1/2}):\left\lVert z-Dh(0)\cdot x\right\rVert_{L^\infty(B_{K\rho_h})}<\frac{\rho_h}{8}\right\}.
\]
These sets cover the restrictions of $\mathcal K$ to $\overline B_{1/2}$. By compactness, we extract a finite subcovering $\mathcal O_{h_1},\ldots,\mathcal O_{h_N}$, with corresponding radii $\rho_1,\ldots,\rho_N$.

We claim that there is a sufficiently small $t_0\in(0,1/2)$ such that, for every solution $v$ in the statement of the lemma, the restriction of $x\mapsto(v(t_0x)-v(0))/t_0$ to $\overline B_{1/2}$ belongs to one of the sets in this finite subcovering. Suppose otherwise. Then, there exist parameters $t_j\in(0,1/2)$ with $t_j\downarrow0$ and solutions $v_j$ as in the statement of the lemma, with shifts $q_j$, such that the functions
\[
u_j(x)\coloneqq\frac{v_j(t_jx)-v_j(0)}{t_j}
\]
satisfy
\[
u_j|_{\overline B_{1/2}}\notin\bigcup_{i=1}^N\mathcal O_{h_i}.
\]
We have $u_j(0)=0$ and
\[
\left\lvert Du_j+q_j\right\rvert(-\Delta)^su_j=0\quad\text{in }B_{1/t_j},
\qquad [u_j]_{C^{0,1}(B_{1/(2t_j)})}\le L.
\]
Using the Lipschitz estimate for $t_j\left\lvert x\right\rvert\le1/2$, and the growth bound for $t_j\left\lvert x\right\rvert > 1/2$, gives
\[
\left\lvert u_j(x)\right\rvert\le(L+4)\left\lvert x\right\rvert+\left\lvert x\right\rvert^{1+\alpha_1}, \quad x\in\mathbb R^n.
\]
Since $1+\alpha_1<2s$, Arzel\`a--Ascoli on expanding balls and dominated convergence give, after passing to a subsequence,
\[
u_j\longrightarrow h\quad\text{locally uniformly in }\mathbb R^n,
\qquad \left\lVert u_j-h\right\rVert_{L_s^1(\mathbb R^n)}\longrightarrow0.
\]
The preceding stability argument shows that $h\in\mathcal K$. Its restriction to $\overline B_{1/2}$ therefore belongs to some $\mathcal O_{h_i}$. By openness and uniform convergence, the same holds for $u_j$, for all sufficiently large $j$, a contradiction. This proves the claim.

Set $\theta\coloneqq t_0\min_i\rho_i$. For a solution $v$ as in the statement of the lemma, choose the element of the subcovering and the corresponding $\rho_i$, and take $r\coloneqq t_0\rho_i$ and $b\coloneqq Dh_i(0)$. Membership in $\mathcal O_{h_i}$ and rescaling give \eqref{eq:nonlocal-affine-approximation}, with $r\in[\theta,\rho_*]$ and $\left\lvert b\right\rvert\le L$.

It remains to verify the growth of $w$. For $\left\lvert x\right\rvert\le K$, \eqref{eq:nonlocal-affine-approximation} and continuity give $\left\lvert w(x)\right\rvert\le1$. If $\left\lvert x\right\rvert>K$ and $r\left\lvert x\right\rvert\le1/2$, then
\[
\left\lvert w(x)\right\rvert\le16L\left\lvert x\right\rvert\le\left\lvert x\right\rvert^{1+\alpha_1}.
\]
If $r\left\lvert x\right\rvert\ge1/2$, the original growth bound gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
\left\lvert v(rx)-v(0)-rb\cdot x\right\rvert
&\le\max\{1,(r\left\lvert x\right\rvert)^{1+\alpha_1}\}+1+Lr\left\lvert x\right\rvert\\
&\le2^{\alpha_1}(4+L)(r\left\lvert x\right\rvert)^{1+\alpha_1}.
\end{aligned}
\]
Thus, by \eqref{eq:nonlocal-choice-of-scales},
\[
\left\lvert w(x)\right\rvert\le8\cdot2^{\alpha_1}(4+L)r^{\alpha_1}\left\lvert x\right\rvert^{1+\alpha_1}\le\left\lvert x\right\rvert^{1+\alpha_1}.
\]
